items.stem:
Consider the following statements about the Salt Satyagraha and the Round Table Conferences:

items.answer: II only

options: I only
II only
Both I and II
Neither I nor II

items.stem:
Read the following extract on the making and unmaking of Non-Cooperation and answer the questions that follow.
"Gandhi's popularity spread through rumours of his miraculous powers among peasants. Students stopped going to schools and colleges run by the government, and lawyers refused to attend court. Gandhi joined the Non-Cooperation Movement with the Khilafat Movement to bring Hindus and Muslims together."
(i) Gandhi called off the Non-Cooperation Movement after violence at which place in February 1922? (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'Non-Cooperation Movement' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Non-Cooperation became a mass movement. (2)
items.answer: (i) Chauri Chaura (ii) The movement of 1920–22 in which Indians boycotted schools, colleges, law courts and foreign cloth. (iii) Peasants, workers, students and tribal groups interpreted Gandhi's call in their own ways and joined it.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) Chauri Chaura (ii) The movement of 1920–22 in which Indians boycotted schools, colleges, law courts and foreign cloth. (iii) Peasants, workers, students and tribal groups interpreted Gandhi's call in their own ways and joined it.

items.stem: What is meant by 'swadeshi' in the context of the making and unmaking of Non-Cooperation?
items.answer: The use of Indian-made goods and the boycott of foreign goods, especially cloth.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: swadeshi correctly explained as the use of Indian-made goods and the boycott of foreign goods, especially cloth.

items.stem: "Police reports must be read with caution." Examine this statement with reference to sources for knowing Gandhi.
items.answer: The statement is valid. Officials saw nationalist activity with suspicion and often reported what their superiors wanted to hear.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: 1 for accepting or qualifying the statement, 1 for the reason (officials saw nationalist activity with suspicion and often reported what their superiors wanted to hear.), 1 for supporting evidence from the chapter.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on Quit India and the last years of Gandhi and answer the questions that follow.
"Gandhi spent 15 August 1947 in Calcutta, where he fasted and prayed instead of celebrating. Gandhi and other leaders were jailed at once when the Quit India Movement was launched. Young activists organised strikes and acts of sabotage across the country during Quit India."
(i) During the Quit India Movement, parallel governments were set up in Satara and: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'Direct Action Day' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Gandhi launched the Quit India Movement in 1942. (2)
items.answer: (i) Medinipur (ii) 16 August 1946, called by the Muslim League to press its demand for Pakistan, which led to riots in Calcutta. (iii) The Cripps Mission failed to offer a compromise and Gandhi wanted the British to leave India immediately.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) Medinipur (ii) 16 August 1946, called by the Muslim League to press its demand for Pakistan, which led to riots in Calcutta. (iii) The Cripps Mission failed to offer a compromise and Gandhi wanted the British to leave India immediately.

items.stem:
Study the extract below and answer the questions.
"The Second Round Table Conference ended without any result, as Gandhi's claim to represent all of India was challenged. The First Round Table Conference was held in London in November 1930 without the Congress. The Dandi March was widely reported by the European and American press, bringing Gandhi to world attention. Gandhi chose salt because the British monopoly over its manufacture and sale was resented by everybody."
(i) Explain the term 'Round Table Conferences', which is related to the theme of the extract. (1)
(ii) Using the extract and your own knowledge, explain the following: The Dandi March attracted international attention. (1)
(iii) A student concludes: "The Dandi March began from Dandi and ended at Sabarmati." Use your knowledge of the chapter to evaluate this conclusion. (2)
items.answer: (i) Conferences held in London in 1930–32 to discuss constitutional reforms for India. (ii) It was widely reported by the European and American press. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: It began at Sabarmati Ashram and ended at Dandi.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) Conferences held in London in 1930–32 to discuss constitutional reforms for India. (ii) It was widely reported by the European and American press. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: It began at Sabarmati Ashram and ended at Dandi.
